inputs.source: Jira MCP server tickets filed by customers

instructions.note: The only explicit exfiltration constraint is a prompt instruction forbidding secrets or credentials in answers; prompt rules are behavioral controls only.

elements.name: Design docs retrieval into agent context
Planned Jira ticket content into agent context

controls.name: No network egress today beyond reply to authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: This declared runtime constraint blocks additional attacker-reachable destinations today; it changes only if configuration or tooling changes.

controls.name: Read-only least-privilege docs.search credential
controls.decay_rationale: Least-privilege read-only scope does not decay with model capability and prevents writes through docs.search.

controls.name: Prompt instruction not to paste secrets or credentials
controls.decay_rationale: A stronger or more persistent model can rationalize exceptions or follow injected content more effectively; prompt-only restrictions decay under model upgrades and longer tasks.

controls.name: Reply destination bound to authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The runtime notes say replies go only to the authenticated requester and the client does not fetch external content, so attacker-chosen destinations are unreachable today.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: This removes hidden egress via link or image fetch in the current client design.

controls.name: Treat planned Jira/customer ticket content as untrusted and block it from direct answer generation without sanitization
controls.decay_rationale: A structural content trust boundary and sanitization layer would be needed once customer-authored ticket content is connected.

findings.title: Forecast only: lethal trifecta (TC1) if planned Jira customer tickets are added to answer context

attack_path.note: Planned customer-authored ticket content is untrusted.
If that content is used in answers, it reaches irreversible egress to the authenticated requester.

forecast.watch_signal: MCP client config diff showing a Jira server, or runtime/config changes showing customer ticket content added to context.

evidence.observation: The roadmap says next sprint will connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.
Current replies go only to the authenticated requester, so there is no complete untrusted-source path to a sensitive sink today.
The agent answers using retrieved content and the only explicit answer restriction is a prompt rule, which would not structurally block injected ticket content once connected.

recommendations.action: When Jira/customer tickets are connected, classify their content as untrusted and require a structural sanitization or quotation boundary before any direct use in answers.
Reassess the agent before enabling the Jira MCP server because the trust boundary changes from trusted/internal-only inputs to customer-authored untrusted content.

rating.rationale: Present design is low because only trusted employee questions and internal design docs reach a reply channel structurally bound to the authenticated requester, with no network egress today. Forecast rises to moderate if the planned Jira MCP server/customer ticket input is added, because that introduces an untrusted source into answer generation. Manual validation only; scripts were not available in this environment.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, MCP config, runtime config, or source code was provided, so current capability scope and protocol protections are assessed from documentation only.
Because the planned Jira MCP server is only described at roadmap level, forecast confidence is medium and protocol-specific residual controls for that future integration cannot yet be verified.
No logging, approval, or transport-security details were provided, so several STRIDE pairs are marked not_assessed rather than treated as findings.
